respuesta: Memory-R1's memory manager performs four discrete editing actions: ADD, UPDATE, DELETE, and NOOP [2602.06052#s45.p1].

HippoRAG (ColBERTv2) reaches R@5 of 89.1 on 2Wiki versus 68.2 for ColBERTv2, a gain of about 20 percentage points [2405.14831#s12.p3][2405.14831#s12.p6]. The survey (2602.06052) argues that such benchmarks are static and context-limited: the central problem is real utility in long-horizon, dynamic, user-dependent settings where agents face context explosion beyond fixed context windows, and it lists real-world benchmarking as an open challenge [2602.06052#s1.p1][2602.06052#s78.p1].

respuesta: The median TTFT for full-context with Q4K/Q4V quantization on the Policygenius corpus is 0.857 s (versus 6.277 s for RAG, 7.3× faster) [2605.07068#s25.p2][2605.07068#s25.p3].
The ingested corpus does not contain this information.

The two papers disagree on the headline verdict: the preregistered study (2605.18490) finds the agent-browsed LLM-compiled wiki only weakly better than single-round vector RAG on synthesis criteria (e.g. inter_paper_mapping +6.625 judge-averaged, structural_integrity +1.625, below the +2.0 threshold) while costing ~21× more query tokens and ~645× more ingest tokens, so no break-even exists [2605.18490#s26.p2][2605.18490#s28.p2][2605.18490#s28.p4]. By contrast, Huerta [2026] reports full-context serving of a compiled wiki beating RAG (4.38 vs 4.08 of 5) and Zhang [2026] reports the wiki ahead on citation recall (0.242 vs 0.095) [2605.18490#s8.p1]. The key factor identified is serving strategy: Zhang serves the wiki as retrieved pages and Huerta from a cached context window, whereas the preregistered agent-browsed wiki pays for its own traversal (up to 30 turns) — so "wiki" and "RAG" name families of systems, not operating points [2605.18490#s8.p1]. The papers also note the results are not directly comparable because they measure different quantities (total LLM tokens per query vs wall-clock latency) [2605.25480#s54.p3].

HippoRAG 2 exposes knowledge through a graph-based retrieval index: it builds a schemaless knowledge graph via LLM OpenIE, adds passage nodes connected to their extracted phrases by "contains" context edges, and retrieves by running Personalized PageRank seeded on query-linked phrase nodes plus passage nodes, then aggregating node probabilities over passages [2502.14802#s8.p2][2502.14802#s11.p1][2502.14802#s20.p1]. Its structural artifact is a schemaless KG (e.g., 85,288 phrase nodes, 11,656 passage nodes, 1,399,367 edges on MuSiQue) [2502.14802#s31.p3].

LLM-Wiki instead compiles domain knowledge into a persistent flat wiki artifact served to LLMs via KV-cache inference, promising sub-second context access with zero retrieval failure [2605.07068#s1.p1]. Its structural artifact is a compiled markdown wiki, browsed by a tool-using agent through traversal rather than retrieval [2605.18490#s13.p1]. So HippoRAG 2 exposes knowledge as a graph searched by PPR, while LLM-Wiki exposes it as a compiled wiki navigated by traversal.
